records.description: Sieur Reichart [?to the baron de Berlepsch]: continuous marches have prevented him from replying to the last three letters. He had hoped to leave immediately to communicate the elector of Bavaria's resolution, but it is impossible to do so now for fear of offending the French, who already have wind of the negotiations. PS. written at Wiblingen, with directions for a secret meeting at Günzburg, near Ulm. Written at camp at Laupheim, between Vienna [probably Ulm is meant] and Biberach, and received in Nuremberg on 10 June. f. 68.

records.context: Secretaries of State: State Papers Foreign, Military Expeditions. Duke of Marlborough.
records.description: Baron de Berlepsch [to Marlborough]: his secret meeting with Sieur Reichart has taken place, and resulted in the enclosed list [ SP 87/2/42 ] of demands by the elector of Bavaria. Reichart showed him a letter from Tallard to the elector: Tallard's army was 35,000 strong, and he had promised the elector assistance with money, provisions and munitions. [Reichart said that] the duke of Savoy was ready to treat with France. Reversals for the allies in Spain, Italy and Hungary. Prince Louis of Baden had made approaches to the elector through a third party, and Prince Eugene was authorized to do so. [Berlepsch] is returning to Berlin, and from thence to Vienna, after which he hopes to visit Marlborough. Dated at Nuremberg. On dorse, copy of a letter [to Berlepsch] at camp at Ober Aching: he welcomes him and requests him to remain hidden. He has found a pretext to meet him in four or five days. ff. 75-78.

records.description: [The baron de] Berlepsch [Prussian minister] [to Marlborough]: he encloses copies from Sieur Reichart, secretary to the elector. He has sent these with the count of Löwenstein, the emperor [Leopold I]'s envoy, asks for an address, and asks that any letters for him should be sent by Buhretti d'Oldfelt, the king's resident in Nuremberg. Dated at Nuremberg. f. 67.
